name: Bathua Paratha
ingredients: Ghee or mustard oil for cooking
instructions: 1. Wash the bathua leaves thoroughly and blanch them in boiling water for 2-3 minutes.
2. Drain the leaves and grind them into a smooth paste.
3. In a large bowl, mix the whole wheat flour, bathua paste, carom seeds, red chili powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, and salt.
4. Knead into a soft, firm dough using the moisture from the bathua paste, adding minimal water if necessary.
5. Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a flat circular disc.
6. Heat a griddle (tawa) and place the rolled paratha on it.
7. Cook on both sides, applying ghee or oil until golden brown spots appear and the paratha is crispy.
description: Bathua Paratha is a quintessential winter breakfast in Haryana. Bathua is a nutritious, wild-growing green leafy vegetable rich in iron and minerals, traditionally harvested during the cold season. It is considered a seasonal superfood that provides warmth and immunity, commonly served with a dollop of white butter (makkhan) and curd.
